pagerduty-bot: [ALERT] High error rate detected for service 'inference-prod' (5xx spike) - Incident #INC-8942 - paging primary on-call

incident-bot: Page fired to schedule 'redwood-inference-oncall' -> responder: maya

maya: ack - I'm looking

emma: wait - why did this page go to maya? sanjay is primary for this window

sanjay: I wasn't paged. I'm primary from 09:00-17:00 today. I see a page to 'inference-prod' in PD, but it shows binding to 'redwood-inference-monitoring' not the oncall schedule we use

jordan: looks like the PD routing rule for the prometheus integration got a duplicate service binding. one binding targets 'inference-prod' properly, the other points to 'inference-nonprod' but with override to the monitoring schedule.

emma: that would cause the page to go to the wrong responder set and also to get auto-resolved by monitoring runbooks. can someone paste the rule?

jordan: pasted snippet from PD UI: ```Rule: Prometheus -> IF alert.match(service=~"inference-.*") THEN route to service: redwood-inference-monitoring (binding id: bnd-73) ELSE route to service: inference-prod (binding id: bnd-72)```

maya: so pd sent page to monitoring binding first, which then forwarded to the monitoring schedule (not the prod oncall). i got it because i'm in monitoring rotation for a different product temporarily. not actually the ML infra owner.

sanjay: and there's an autoresolve configured on the monitoring binding: if metric clears within 2m, mark resolved. that explains why PD auto-resolved INC-8942 while the underlying error flapped. we missed customer impact initially.

emma: action plan: 1) stop further wrong pages (disable bnd-73) 2) confirm primary oncall gets notified 3) assess customer impact and open a follow-up SR/communication 4) postmortem to adjust PD rule matching regex.

jordan: disabling bnd-73 now in PD console... done.

pagerduty-bot: Binding bnd-73 disabled by jordan at 2026-03-14T15:12:28Z

sanjay: rerun alert test from prometheus: ```curl -XPOST https://prom-alerts.example.internal/test -d '{"service":"inference-prod","severity":"critical"}'```

incident-bot: Test alert fired -> Incident #INC-8943 created -> pager sent to schedule 'redwood-inference-oncall' -> responder: sanjay

sanjay: ack. I have the new page. verifying logs and traces now.

maya: sorry for the confusion. I was going to escalate but the autoresolve made it look low severity. glad we caught the routing mismatch.

emma: initial customer impact: 3 customers reported elevated 500 errors for ~7 minutes during the spike window. several requests fell back to cached responses, no data loss. ops team: estimate 5-10% of inference requests had transient failures.

jordan: digging into infra logs - the error spike coincided with a hot-restart of a GPU worker pool causing partial KV cache invalidation. retries caused the 5xx waterfall.

sanjay: mitigation: rolled back the recent autoscaler tweak for that pool, restarted unhealthy pods, and increased retry jitter. error rates trending down.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-8942 auto-resolved (bindings changed). Historically linked incidents: INC-8943 (test).

emma: follow-ups (owners):
- PD routing audit (jordan) - look for duplicate bindings and autoresolve combos
- Oncall schedule verification (ops) - confirm no overlaps with monitoring schedules
- Postmortem and customer comms (emma + sanjay)

maya: +1 on the audit. I'll volunteer to review the monitoring runbooks so we don't have cross-targeted autoresolves.

jordan: created PD ticket TKT-4021 to remove legacy binding and add a regex test suite for rule matching. ETA EOD tomorrow.

emma: note for postmortem: include timeline of pages, autoresolve events, and customer impact with exact counts. also propose a PD rule linter as part of infra hygiene.

sanjay: closing loop - error rate back to baseline, no more pages. adding postmortem label and will schedule a 30-min triage sync tomorrow.

maya: thanks team. lesson learned: PD bindings can be dangerously sticky when legacy configs exist. we'll add a weekly PD rule audit to eng-sre cadence. :white_check_mark:
